content: 1. High doses of folic acid (1 mg/day or more) may obscure the detection of vitamin B12 deficiency. Specifically, folic acid supplementation can correct the hematological manifestations of B12 deficiency, such as pernicious anemia, without addressing the associated neurological symptoms. 2. L-methylfolate is less likely than folic acid to mask a vitamin B12 deficiency. 3. Pregnancy Category C: There is insufficient evidence to determine whether this product is safe for use during pregnancy. 4. Lactation: It is unknown whether this product is excreted in breast milk. 5. Pregnancy Category A: Generally considered acceptable. Controlled studies in pregnant women have not demonstrated any risk to the fetus. 6. Pharmacokinetics: The peak plasma concentration of the product is 129 ng/mL at 3 hours post-administration. The area under the curve (AUC) is 383 mcg•h/mL. Approximately 56% of the product is protein-bound. 7. Volume of distribution (Vd): The product exhibits wide distribution, with red blood cell folate levels remaining elevated for over 40 days after discontinuation of supplementation. 8. Half-life: The elimination half-life of the product is approximately 3 hours. 9. Excretion: The product is primarily excreted via the urine. 10. In the United States, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. 11. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. For less severe cases, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 12. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 13. This information was last revised in May 2024. 14.
